title: AuthenticationAssurance
description: Descriptive information about how a principal authenticated for the current context -- not a business authorization grant (ADR-0015 §180). Consumers use this to decide whether a risk-sensitive operation's AssuranceRequirement (assurance-requirement.schema.json) is met, not to authorize the operation itself. acr is the required assurance context; amr is optional authentication-method evidence. Both are issuer-authenticated: a browser never asserts either. A provider that proves a strong authentication through its acr alone (for example a LoA reserved for a WebAuthn-only flow) need not emit amr, and no provider is required to add a custom extension just to emit one.

acr.description: OIDC Authentication Context Class Reference for this authentication event, as asserted by the issuer. This is the assurance context; its meaning (for example a level reserved for a phishing-resistant flow) is defined by the issuer's flow configuration and mapped to a canonical Baobab level by the consuming policy.

amr.description: OIDC Authentication Methods References used to establish this authentication (e.g. pwd, webauthn, otp). Optional method evidence: present when the issuer can attest the methods, absent otherwise. Absence is not evidence of a weak method; a requirement that needs a method and finds no amr is satisfied only through an accepted acr (see AssuranceRequirement.accepted_acr_values).

authenticated_at.description: When the underlying authentication event occurred (OIDC auth_time).

step_up_at.description: When a step-up re-authentication most recently occurred, if any (ADR-0015 §37-39).

issuer.description: The verified OIDC issuer that authenticated this principal.

client_id.description: The OAuth client (azp) the authentication was performed for.
